FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 302
Committee: Veterans, Military Affairs, and Sponsor: Senator Sam Givhan
Public Safety
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 02/24/2026
Senate Bill 302 as introduced would authorize Marion Military Institute (MMI) to establish a
new associate degree program incorporating the Alabama Peace Officers' Standards and
Training Commission's basic training curriculum required for certification as a law enforcement
officer. This would increase the obligations of MMI by an undetermined amount to update
existing curriculum, hire additional institutional personnel for the new program, and to issue a
Provisional Alabama Law Enforcement Officer Certification upon graduation to each individual
completing the program which could be offset, in part or in whole, by the tuition and fees
charged by MMI upon students enrolling in the program.
In addition, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama Peace
Officers' Standards and Training Commission (APOST) to; (1) recognize MMI as an Alabama
law enforcement training academy; (2) adopt rules, in conjunction with MMI, to implement and
administer the program; and (3) adopt rules to implement and administer the provisional
certification process.
Lastly, this bill could decrease future basic academy training costs paid by law enforcement
agencies for individuals attending other APOST law enforcement training academies, by an
undetermined amount dependent upon the number of MMI cadets that complete the program
and are hired on a full-time basis as a fully certified law enforcement officer.
